newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn intelligence made Iran verdict possible - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn intelligence made Iran verdict possible - paper.

text.p: Information gathered by Germany's BND intelligence service made possible the verdict of a Berlin court that Tehran's leaders ordered the 1992 killing of Kurdish dissidents, a German newspaper said on Friday.
"Without the information of the BND there would have been no Mykonos trial," the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung quoted a source close to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office as saying.
A German court on Thursday accused Iran's political leadership of ordering the killings of a group of Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.
The chancellor's office, Germany's counter-intelligence agency, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) and the BND all declined to comment on the report.
The court ruling prompted Germany to expel four Iranian diplomats and the European Union has invited member countries to recall ambassadors and break off a "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Iran, which condemned the verdict and denied it was involved in terrorism, ordered out four German diplomats.

The Frankfurter Allgemeine said the BND had gained the names of those behind the attack and other information from a "high-ranking Iranian source", and passed it on to German prosecutors investigating the case.
It said the BfV and BND had organised the "the biggest postwar telephone tapping operation" and monitored all calls between Germany and Iran since late last year.
Government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told a regular news conference he knew nothing about the report, but said he found it hard to imagine it could be true.
The paper said the lack of Farsi speakers among the BND's 50 telephone tappers meant the service could only listen in to conversations held in English or German.

It said security sources had confirmed that all telephone, fax and telex traffic from Iran's embassy in Bonn had been monitored and said authorities were instructed to investigate possible preparations for attacks by Iran.
The BfV last month said it feared violence -- in Iran and Germany -- when the Berlin court ruled on the assassinations.
The paper said the BND had resumed relations with the Iranian secret service in the late 1980s and Tehran had allowed it to set up a residence there.

But the BND pulled its agents out of Tehran in March last year, just before the Berlin court issued an arrest warrant for Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan, whom prosecutors accuse of masterminding the murders.
